speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming your sudden onset of vertigo. To help me pinpoint the cause, have you noticed any accompanying symptoms like hearing loss, tinnitus, or double vision? Also, have you had any recent head trauma or severe headaches?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The brief duration of symptoms (3 minutes), lack of hearing loss or neurological deficits, and onset while changing position are classic for displaced otoconia in the inner ear.
